title: Association of Taiwanese Students at MIT
content_html:
The Association of Taiwanese Students (ATS) at MIT is an undergraduate student organization founded in 1991 to celebrate and explore Taiwanese culture on campus. According to the organization’s own history, ATS was established that year when a student had the idea of forming a group devoted to activities related to Taiwanese culture, at a time when MIT’s existing Chinese student organizations were seen as serving a different function. The club is listed among MIT’s officially recognized multicultural student organizations and maintains an active website at mitats.org.

ATS consists primarily of undergraduate students with Taiwanese heritage or an interest in Taiwanese culture, though membership is open to the entire MIT community regardless of background. Signature events include the Lunar New Year Banquet, Nightmarket — described on the organization’s website as MIT’s largest Asian celebration — pineapple cake (鳳梨酥) making workshops, and boba-making socials. The club also maintains a family system, with members joining named “famlines” that carry on traditions across class years. An executive board manages events and club operations, and a restored wiki serves as an archive of ATS history.
